Found and fixed a real figure-drop bug in render_page.py itself (not just latex.py): render_group()'s use of flow_text_join() (which explicitly skips figure segments - it exists for prompt/answer text where a nested figure would be unusual) silently dropped any figure nested INSIDE a solution block's flow, rendering nothing in its place with no visible sign anything was missing. Caught via the mandatory figure-count check (distinct figure_srcs: JSON said 5, first HTML render only had 4) - ex_2.2's चित्र 2.7 (referenced mid-sentence inside its own :::concept, not as an item-level :::figure) was the dropped one. physics-12-1 never exercised this path (confirmed: no item in its own JSON has a figure nested in a solution flow), so the gap was latent there, not previously caught. Fixed by adding render_flow_content() - walks a flow preserving order, renders text segments as before and figure segments as a proper s76-s79 figure element in their correct position - and using it everywhere flow_text_join() was previously used for solution/note content (prompt/answer flows still use flow_text_join, correctly, since a figure there would be unusual and out of scope for this fix). Re-verified: 5/5 figure srcs resolve after the fix, tag balance clean, 37/37 question/final_answer numbers present, 0 leftover bare LaTeX command names. Also found and fixed (during the manual PDF read-back, not the HTML read-back - this is really a stage-10 export-pipeline fix but discovered and applied here since stage 9's own read-back surfaced it): Chromium's print/PDF text-shaping pipeline mis-renders Devanagari pre-base vowel-sign reordering (े/ि) for text whose nearest explicitly-font-sized ancestor differs from its own font-size - .s3 (chapter title, 38px) nested under .s1 (12.5px base) produced visibly garbled text ('स्थिरवैद्युत' etc.) in the exported PDF despite rendering perfectly correctly on-screen and in the source HTML text itself (confirmed via repr() - no data corruption, purely a PDF-rasterization defect). physics-12-1's own title never exercised this since none of its words need pre-base reordering. Root-caused via ~10 isolated test pages (documented in scratchpad font_test*.html/css) before landing on the actual fix: forcing page.emulate_media(media='screen') immediately before page.pdf() in the export script sidesteps the buggy print-shaping path entirely (page.pdf() still paginates via @page regardless of media type, and @media print's own CSS override wasn't actually load-bearing for layout here) - verified this produces byte-identical page count (21) and dimensions (A4) with the title now rendering correctly and no other visible regression. This belongs properly in stage 10's export script/manifest (documented there); mentioned here since it was this stage's own mandatory read-back that caught it. Defensively also added 'Noto Serif Devanagari' as an explicit font-family fallback ahead of 'STIX Two Text' on .s3/.s12/.s71/.s73 in this chapter's final.hi.css (STIX Two Text has no Devanagari coverage at all) - this did NOT fix the garbling on its own (confirmed by direct test) but is still correct defensive practice independent of the emulate_media fix.

Mechanical export via Playwright/Chromium exactly per step_10/PROMPT.md's recipe (networkidle + document.fonts.ready + prefer_css_page_size + print_background), with one addition: page.emulate_media(media='screen') called immediately before page.pdf(). This fixes a real Chromium PDF-export bug (found and root-caused during stage 9's own read-back, documented in full there): the default print-media text-shaping pipeline mis-renders Devanagari pre-base vowel-sign reordering (े/ि) for text whose nearest explicitly-font-sized ancestor differs from its own font-size (this chapter's title, .s3 at 38px nested under .s1's 12.5px base, came out visibly garbled - 'स्थिरवैद्युत' etc. - despite the underlying HTML text being byte-correct, confirmed via repr()). Forcing screen-media emulation makes page.pdf() use the (unaffected) screen shaping path instead - page.pdf() still paginates via @page regardless of the emulated media type, and this chapter's @media print override turned out not to be load-bearing for layout (page count and A4 dimensions confirmed unchanged with vs. without the emulate_media call). physics-12-1 never hit this since none of its own title/heading text needed pre-base vowel reordering - this is now a standing fix for every future chapter's export script, not a one-off patch, since any Hindi chapter's title could contain a word needing this reordering. Documented in step_10/PROMPT.md as a new trap.
